root_idea.summary: The root centers on the entry of one thing into another, especially entry into an interior or confined space.
root_idea.development: The physical idea of entering extends to penetration, causing one thing to enter or overlap another, and figuratively admitting an outsider into an inner circle or relying on such an associate. Related nouns designate places of entry or shelter, repeated entering, and things or persons affected by entry.

senses.definition: To enter into or penetrate a place or thing, including by passing through an opening into its interior.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic uses include entry into a constricted opening and entry into the earth or other created domains; the verb is not restricted to a particular type of object.

senses.definition: To cause one thing to enter into another; to make it overlap or encroach upon it.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic usage this is especially applied to the reciprocal increase of night and day, as a portion of one is made to enter into and extend the other.

senses.definition: An outsider admitted as an intimate or trusted associate, or taken as an object of reliance despite not belonging to one's own people.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in the Quranic construction of taking someone or something as a وليجة; the referent may be a person or another external entity, and the emphasis is on inner association or reliance outside the proper circle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To insert the penis; hence, to have sexual intercourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional Form IV construction distinct from the Quranic use concerning the interpenetration of night and day.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who frequently goes out and comes in.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive noun or epithet for repeated movement outward and inward.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sheltered place or cavern where travelers take refuge from rain and the like; also a bend or recessed place in a valley.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The valley sense concerns a physical turn or recess and is related to the notion of an inward or sheltered place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Anything introduced or inserted into something without belonging to it; an outsider or adherent admitted among a group without being one of its members.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This broader Classical usage covers an inserted thing as well as a person included among others; the Quranic intimate or trusted associate is a specialized usage of the same headword.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A disease or pain affecting the abdomen; in some lexical reports, a pain affecting the teeth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sources preserve variation concerning the precise bodily location of the pain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More or most penetrating, said of language or discourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A comparative or superlative adjective applied to the penetrating quality of speech or expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hiding place among trees into which a wild animal enters.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term denotes a concealed animal refuge, not merely any general place of entry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place of entrance or a place into which one enters.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place noun, with a plural مَوَالِج.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person afflicted by the disease called وَالِجَة or دُبَيْلَة.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-result noun referring to the person affected by that disease.
Reported as an extension associated with the root's basic notion of entering.

cautions: وَلِيجَة in the Quranic verse is variously explained as an outsider admitted into confidence, a non-family confidant, or specifically an intimate associated with polytheists; these interpretations share the core idea of an external associate taken as an inner reliance.
